Subject: Oakmont RFP — Offline/Isolated Deployment questions (Annex B)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking our Annex B for review. A few clarifications we need as we evaluate private (air-gapped) deployment feasibility for Oakmont:

1) Can Redwood perform a fully disconnected install (no outbound internet) for model hosting? If so, what components require one-time outbound access (if any) and what are the recommended mitigations?
2) Describe the recommended key management architecture for customer-owned keys (KMS/HSM). Specifically: key rotation, key wrapping for model artifacts, and offline backup handling.
3) We need an operational rollback procedure for patch/upgrade failures when nodes have no external access. Please include detection and remediation windows.
4) Requirements for evidence during an audit: what logs/artifacts do you provide (audit with timestamps, immutable storage, chain-of-custody notes)?

I've attached Annex B (Oakmont_RFP_Annex_B.xlsx) with our baseline questionnaire. We're trying to finalize vendor fit by next week.

Can you confirm whether you can answer these in-line or if you'd prefer a short technical workshop?

Thanks,

—Elena Morris
Director, Technology Sourcing
Oakmont Health Systems

Subject: Re: Oakmont RFP — Offline/Isolated Deployment questions (Annex B)

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Below are concise answers; happy to expand in a workshop and to provide redlines for SLAs.

1) Disconnected install capability
- Yes: Redwood supports fully air-gapped installs for model serving. Our private appliance stack (customer-managed) can operate without any outbound network egress once images and model artifacts are deployed into the environment.
- One-time outbound requirements (optional): For convenience we offer an initial image signature check via our verification service. This is optional — customers can perform an offline signature verification check using the published signing keys we provide in the install bundle.
- Mitigations: provide install bundle on encrypted media, use vendor-supplied signing keys, and perform local checksum verification.

2) Customer-owned KMS/HSM architecture
- Supported patterns: (a) Local HSM with PKCS#11, (b) Cloud KMS with offline key wrap delivered via secure transfer, (c) Bring-your-own-HSM with remote attestation.
- Key rotation: Rotation is orchestrated by a customer-managed rotation service; Redwood provides hooks for re-wrapping model disk encryption keys and updating runtime configuration without requiring model re-serialization. Rotation operations can be executed during a maintenance window; we provide an automation runbook.
- Key wrapping for model artifacts: Models are encrypted at rest with a data key that is wrapped by the customer KMS key. We store only the wrapped key in our local metadata store.
- Offline backups: Encrypted snapshots are stored on customer-controlled media. We publish a verifiable manifest and checksum for each snapshot to support chain-of-custody.

3) Offline upgrade/rollback procedure
- Detection: Runtime health monitors (local) detect degraded process states and surface events to the ops console (local-only).
- Rollback: Each upgrade is shipped with a validated rollback image and an idempotent rollback script. In offline mode, rollback is executed via the bundled playbook (we include both automated and manual runbook paths). Typical remediation window: 10–30 minutes for single-node rollback; cluster-wide coordinated rollback depends on model shard size — usually under 2 hours for our standard configurations.
- We will provide a playbook (offline_rollback_playbook.docx) and a short test plan you can execute in a staging air-gapped environment.

4) Audit evidence and logs
- Audit artifacts we provide: immutable activity log (append-only), signed install manifests, time-stamped model lineage records, and access audit (who/when). Logs are exported to a customer-controlled archive in a format compliant with common SIEM ingestion (JSONL or syslog).
- Chain-of-custody: Each artifact is accompanied by a signed manifest and checksum. For higher-assurance engagements, we can provide notarized manifests via third-party signing.

Attachments included: redwood_airgap_install_guide_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB), kv_cache_network_diagram.png (PNG, 420KB), offline_rollback_playbook.docx (DOCX, 120KB)

Next steps
- If the answers look reasonable, propose a 90-minute technical workshop this week to walk through the offline install and run our staged rollback test. Please share your preferred times.

Best,

—Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Rishi — thanks for the rapid response. Couple quick clarifications before we book a workshop: 

- For the rollback playbook: can you confirm whether the rollback path requires any signature verification from Redwood's signing service (i.e., will we need network access to validate or can we validate using the offline signing keys you provide)?
- For key rotation and traceability: do you expose an auditable key version history (who rotated when) that can be exported for our auditors?
- Identity integration: what is the recommended approach for SCIM/SAML provisioning in an air-gapped environment — do you support a local IDP connector, or do customers need to provide a proxy sync mechanism?

If you can answer these three in-line we can decide whether to run the staged rollback in our lab or have Redwood lead the test.

—Simon
